source.quote: Shanling's own manual for the UA1 II, UA1II.pdf, read 2026-11-25 - the product page is image-only, so the manual is the source. Its numbered feature list: « 1. True Double DAC setup with Cirrus Logic CD43131 DACs. » « 2. Hi-Res PCM support up to 32bit / 768kHz. » « 3. Native DSD support up to DSD512. » Menu settings: Filter.

facts.chip: « True Double DAC setup with Cirrus Logic CD43131 DACs » - « CD43131 » is the manual's spelling, almost certainly for CS43131, and it is not corrected here.

device_settings.why: The manual's menu table gives item « Filter » with options « F0-F4 » - five filters, numbered and NOT named. The English table prints no names at all.

_la_source_est_une_annonce_ou_un_manuel_: Shanling's product pages are image-only, so every figure comes from the maker's own announcement at /article/NNNNNN or from its manual PDF, both on en.shanling.com. No number was read off an image, and nothing is sourced to store.shanling.com. See the brand file.
_le_mot_NATIF_vient_du_manuel_et_nest_pa: « Native DSD support up to DSDnnn » is the manual's own wording, in a numbered feature list, and it appears in every UA manual in the same form. It is NOT the boilerplate that had to be refused on xDuoo, where one sentence was repeated on twenty unrelated pages including a passive module: here it sits on a family of dongles whose only digital input is the USB-C port it describes, and the figure varies by model - DSD256 on the UA1 Plus and UA1s, DSD512 on the rest. A claim that varies with the product is a claim about the product. DoP is never mentioned for any UA model.
_une_puce_ecrite_CD43131_dans_trois_manu: The UA1 II, UA6 and UA6 II manuals all print « Cirrus Logic CD43131 », while the UA6 II's own announcement prints « 8x Cirrus Logic CS43131 DACs ». CS43131 is a part that exists; CD43131 is not. The manual's spelling is quoted as printed on each record and the announcement's is quoted here, which gives a reader both without this catalogue deciding which of the maker's two spellings is the slip.
